damage: Crowds out native plants and is a preferred host for spotted lanternflies.
safe_action: Do not simply cut mature trees: roots can produce new shoots. Photograph, map, and ask a trained professional about integrated control and native replacement.

damage: Climbs and damages trees by shading and weighing down branches.
safe_action: Record the location. Join a supervised vine-control effort; avoid pulling large vines out of tree canopies.

damage: Displaces forest plants and may create conditions favorable to ticks.
safe_action: Wear protective clothing and remove small plants with roots where permitted. Coordinate larger removal and restore native shrubs.

damage: Forms dense stands that displace vegetation and affect riparian habitats.
safe_action: Do not dig up and transport roots or stem pieces. Refer established patches for a multi-year management plan.

damage: Displaces native wetland plants and changes habitat.
safe_action: Photograph and map patches. Work with wetland managers; pulling in protected wetlands may require permission.

damage: Non-native lineages form dense stands that displace native marsh plants.
safe_action: Request professional identification of the invasive lineage before removal; coordinate permitted wetland control.

damage: Crowds out native wildflowers and can interfere with forest soil fungi.
safe_action: For small patches, obtain landowner permission and pull before seeds develop; bag plants appropriately.

damage: Creates thorny thickets that crowd out native plants.
safe_action: Use gloves and tools for small shrubs on permitted sites; seek help for large thickets.

damage: Spreads through field edges and crowds out native shrubs.
safe_action: Map and remove small seedlings where permitted; coordinate management for mature seed-bearing shrubs.

damage: Shades native forest seedlings and understory flowers.
safe_action: Join approved shrub removal and native planting projects.

damage: Spreads through wet woods and crowds out native seedlings.
safe_action: Control seedlings and large bushes through a coordinated plan; revisit for new seedlings.

damage: Spreads underground to replace ground-layer plants.
safe_action: Avoid transferring contaminated soil and roots. Follow repeated, careful control over multiple seasons.

damage: Displaces native shoreline and wetland plants.
safe_action: Avoid skin contact with plant sap. Ask wetland managers about permitted removal.

damage: Escapes from landscaping and can outcompete native trees.
safe_action: Avoid planting; work with property owners to replace escaped trees with native species.

damage: Forms dense underwater growth that affects recreation and native plant habitats.
safe_action: Clean, drain, and dry boats. Do not fragment or transport plants; refer patches to lake managers.
numerical_extent: About 35 acres documented in Lake Quinsigamond in 2019

damage: Displaces native aquatic vegetation and affects recreation.
safe_action: Clean, drain, and dry equipment. Lake managers determine permitted treatments.
numerical_extent: About 6 acres documented in Lake Quinsigamond in 2019

damage: Can grow into dense stands that limit native aquatic plants and recreation.
safe_action: Avoid creating plant fragments; inform the lake-management team.
numerical_extent: About 5 acres documented in Lake Quinsigamond in 2019

damage: Can form beds that compete with other aquatic plants.
safe_action: Monitor and prevent boat-assisted spread; coordinate management with lake authorities.
numerical_extent: About 1 acre documented in Lake Quinsigamond in 2019

damage: Can cover water surfaces and restrict habitat and recreation.
safe_action: Participate only in supervised hand-pulling projects; collect plants before seeds form.

damage: Can compete with native aquatic plants and cause seasonal surface growth.
safe_action: Report suspected patches. Early-season surveys may be needed to confirm them.

damage: Can form dense stands in shallow water; extent depends on location.
safe_action: Monitor with lake managers; do not remove native look-alikes or undertake unpermitted shoreline work.
numerical_extent: About 0.1 acres documented in Lake Quinsigamond in 2019

damage: Forms dense underwater vegetation in infested water bodies.
safe_action: Prevent transport on boats and equipment; submit suspected occurrences for expert verification.

damage: Feeds on plant sap, produces honeydew and can damage vines and trees.
safe_action: Photograph it, check vehicles and outdoor equipment, and use the official Massachusetts reporting guidance. Do not apply pesticides without expert guidance.

damage: Larvae kill ash trees, creating hazardous dead trees and removal expenses.
safe_action: Have ash trees inspected by an arborist; approved treatment can protect selected trees. Avoid moving potentially infested firewood.

damage: Larvae tunnel into hardwood trees and can kill them.
safe_action: Photograph suspected beetles and emergence holes. Report to agricultural or forestry authorities; do not transport suspect wood.

damage: Weakens eastern hemlock trees by feeding on sap.
safe_action: Monitor hemlock branches for white woolly patches; refer severe infestations to arborists.

damage: Caterpillars defoliate and can kill boxwood shrubs.
safe_action: Photograph caterpillars and damage. Follow official state reporting and approved control guidance.

damage: Larvae eat elm leaves in zigzag patterns, reducing tree health.
safe_action: Record photos of leaf damage and report to forest-health authorities.

damage: Damages leaves and can kill American beech trees.
safe_action: Photograph leaf striping and consult a professional; do not use unapproved treatments.

damage: Changes topsoil structure and can harm forest understory plants.
safe_action: Avoid transferring soil, mulch, or worms between locations. Exact species requires expert identification.

damage: Competes with native aquatic organisms and may alter water ecosystems.
safe_action: Clean, drain, and dry boats and gear; report suspected new locations.
